nodes.title: Note: How to use (members)
widgets_values:
## FastH3 Omni Talking Character (members) - a director's workflow
Think like a director: **cast** your character once, then shoot **shot after shot**. Same face, same voice, new places.

**1 Cast: character** - **Picture 1** is who they are (face + outfit; a plain background works best: the background is NOT reused). **Character** describes them in words (age, hair, clothes).

**2 Cast: voice** - give the character a voice ONCE, save it, reuse it forever:
- **Design a voice** (row 2, on by default): describe the voice in words ("a deep, calm male voice, slight rasp") - no recording needed. Run once, listen to **Hear the designed voice**, change the seed until you like it.
- or **Clone a voice from a sample** (row 2): a clean 5-15 s recording + its exact words.
- **Save it** under the character's name (Save node, filename). Then press **R** to refresh, switch **Use a saved voice** ON and the maker OFF (muter in group 5), and pick the name. Every shot from now on uses that exact voice.

**3 Shot** - one clip = one shot: **Location** (where), **Shot** (wide / medium / close-up + camera move), **Action** (what they do, their expression), **Line** (what they say), **Mood hint** (optional: nudges the voice a little; it will not whisper or shout), **Duration** (at least as long as the line), size (0.6 MP for 12 GB cards).
**Keep faces big:** at 0.6 MP use medium shots and closer (faces far from the camera come out soft); for a wide shot switch the size to 1 MP.
Location picture: switch on **Picture 2: location** and write "the place shown in <Picture 2>" in Location, so a set looks the same in every shot.

**4 The line** - **Listen to the line** first (right-click > Queue Selected Output Nodes, about 10 s). Different take? change the seed; keep it to keep the take. Then **Run**: the video reuses that exact take, lips in sync.

**Next shot:** keep the cast (picture, saved voice, seed), change the Shot fields. Write each shot like a script line: where, framing, action, line.
**Optional extras** (group 5 switches): Picture 2 (location), Reference Video, Your Audio (your own recording instead of the voice take: switch group 4 off), RTX 2x Upscale. **Engine** (bottom): already set.

**Measured on an RTX 4000 Ada (20 GB):** a short line takes about 7-10 s to voice; a 5 s clip at 0.6 MP samples in about 2 minutes.
Only use voices and faces you have the rights to, never to impersonate or deceive anyone, and label your results as AI-generated.
FastH3 Omni by FastVideo + Nuva Lab, based on MiniMax H3 by MiniMax (MiniMax-H3 Community License: read it, it limits where outputs may be used). Qwen3-TTS by Alibaba Qwen (Apache-2.0). Video by TheLocalLab: youtube.com/@TheLocalLab

nodes.title: Note: Model Links
widgets_values:
## Model Links

**FastH3 Omni** (FastVideo) - https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastH3-Omni-Comfy/tree/main
- diffusion_models/fasth3_omniref_8step_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors (~22 GB) -> ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/
  - or the bf16 version (~44 GB) if you have the RAM

**Text encoder + VAEs** (same files as MiniMax H3) - https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/main
- text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors (~16 GB) -> ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/
  - fast NVFP4 needs an RTX 50 series card; it also runs on older cards (we use it on RTX 30/40-class GPUs). The int8 version (~27 GB) is the other option.
- vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors (~2.8 GB) -> ComfyUI/models/vae/
- vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors (~0.6 GB) -> ComfyUI/models/vae/ (needed for the sound)

**Custom nodes:** the main nodes are built into ComfyUI (update to the latest version). For the optional groups: VideoHelperSuite (reference video, 2x save), Nvidia RTX Nodes (upscale), rgthree (group switch). Install with ComfyUI Manager -> Install Missing Custom Nodes.

## Members: voice models + node
- **Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base** (voice cloning, Alibaba Qwen, Apache-2.0) - https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base/tree/main -> ComfyUI/models/qwen-tts/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base/ (4.54 GB)
- **Qwen3-TTS 1.7B VoiceDesign** (design a voice from a description) - https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-VoiceDesign/tree/main -> ComfyUI/models/qwen-tts/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-VoiceDesign/ (4.3 GB)
- **Qwen3-TTS Tokenizer 12Hz** - https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-Tokenizer-12Hz/tree/main -> ComfyUI/models/qwen-tts/Qwen3-TTS-Tokenizer-12Hz/ (0.68 GB)
- Low VRAM: **Qwen3-TTS 0.6B Base** - https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base/tree/main -> ComfyUI/models/qwen-tts/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base/ (2.52 GB)
- Node: ComfyUI-Qwen-TTS (by flybirdxx). The members installer sets up the node and downloads the models.

nodes.title: Note: Sizes and Speed
widgets_values:
## Sizes and Speed

| megapixels | 16:9 | 9:16 | 1:1 | 2:3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6 | 1056 x 608 | 608 x 1056 | 768 x 768 | 640 x 960 |
| 0.8 | 1216 x 672 | 672 x 1216 | 896 x 896 | 736 x 1120 |
| 1.0 | 1376 x 768 | 768 x 1376 | 1024 x 1024 | 832 x 1248 |

Measured on an RTX 4000 Ada (20 GB), 5 s, 8 steps, sparse attention on: 0.6 MP about 1:50-2:07 (12 GB limit: full speed, peak 11.3 GB); 1 MP about 3:05-3:14 (peak 12.8 GB under a 13.5 GB limit). A full Task Manager is normal: ComfyUI fills free VRAM on purpose.

Duration: 5 s = 124 frames (the model's trained range is about 5-15 s). The RTX 2x Upscale group doubles the final size.

nodes.title: Picture 2: location (a set that must match across shots)
Reference video (2-15 s; its look and motion)
Your audio (the exact line the character speaks)
Note: Prompt Guide
widgets_values:
## Prompt Guide (the format FastH3 Omni was trained on)

Name each reference with its tag in the order they are connected: <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, <Video 1>, <Audio 1>.

**One picture -> new scene, two shots** (the example in this workflow: the hangar): subject_definitions (who/what is in <Picture 1>), summary starting with [reference generation], retention_analysis (what must stay the same), detailed_description with [Shot 1] (and [Shot 2] at 00:02.500 for a cut), overall_soundscape (the sounds you want), non_diegetic_music (N/A or a style).

**Lip-sync to YOUR audio** (switch on "Your Audio"; your line is played 1:1):
- subject_definitions: add "<Audio 1> is the complete dialogue track for <Subject 1> (S1), a clear spoken English male voice."
- summary: start with [reference generation + audio reuse]
- retention_analysis: add "<Audio 1>: fully_copy - <Audio 1> is reused 1:1 as the target video's complete final audio track."
- detailed_description: write the exact words inside <d>[English] ...</d>, e.g. <Subject 1> (S1) looks into the camera and says, <d>[English] Your exact line here.</d> Then he closes his mouth and nods.
- Make the clip at least as long as your audio (pad the audio with silence to the clip length).

**Reference video:** "<Subject 1> is the fox in <Video 1>: ..." then describe the NEW scene. The video sets the look and motion; it is not copied.

Tips: one clear action per shot; describe the sounds you want; end each spoken line with a period.

nodes.title: Listen to the line (queue this first)
Note: Voice
widgets_values:
## Voice
- **Saved voices** live in ComfyUI/models/qwen-tts/voices/ (name.qvp + .wav + .json). Press **R** after saving to see a new one.
- **Same voice every shot:** the saved voice + the same **seed** in Speak the line. A new seed = a new take of the same voice.
- **Mood hint** (group 3) goes to the voice as a style instruction ("tense", "tired"). In our tests it changed the take a little but did NOT make a real whisper or shout: put the emotion in the Action box (the face) and pick the take by seed.
- **Language:** set it in Speak the line (10 languages) and write the Line in that language.
- **model_choice 1.7B** (0.6B for low VRAM, same speed); **attention sdpa**; **unload_model_after_generate on** (frees the GPU for the video model).
